newsitem.title: KENYA: Nine killed in Zaire air raid, says aid worker.
newsitem.headline: Nine killed in Zaire air raid, says aid worker.

text.p: At least nine people were killed and up to 37 wounded when three Zairean government jets bombed the rebel-held east Zaire city of Bukavu on Monday, the medical charity Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF-Holland) said.

The bombing was the first government aerial attack confirmed by independent sources since rebels launched a military campaign last October and seized a large swath of territory in the vast central African nation.
Marcel van Soest, head of MSF in the rebel headquarters of Goma, told Reuters by telephone that his staff had counted the dead and wounded at a local hospital in Bukavu.
"According to our people on the ground, who are currently working in the hospital treating the wounded, there are nine confirmed dead and 37 wounded," he said.
"Of the wounded, between 15 and 20 were mild cases and the rest were serious," he added.
He said the MSF team was working with experts from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). More medical supplies for the wounded were being brought to Bukavu hospital, he said.

An eyewitness, another aid worker who declined to be identified, earlier told Reuters that six people were killed and as many as 20 wounded when the jets pounded Bukavu, the largest city in Zaires Kivu region.
The eyewitness said he counted the dead and wounded after the bombing.

"Among the dead were a very young child about 14 months old and one woman," he said, adding that the bombs dug holes three metres deep (10 feet) when they fell around Bukavu market and near the governors residence.
He said many Bukavu residents were fleeing the city with belongings on their heads, heading towards surrounding hills. Rebel radio broadcast appeals for calm.
Van Soest told Reuters the bombing lasted five minutes, just after 1400 GMT.
He said three jets dropped several bombs in Bukavu, the capital of South Kivu province.
"Several bombs, but we do not know how many (were dropped). Planes came from the west, bombing lasted five minutes," he said.

Zaires ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko has refused to negotiate with Laurent Kabilas rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire and instead has promised to hit back at the rebels.
The central government in Kinshasa accuses Kabila of waging a proxy war for neighbouring Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi. All three deny Zaires charges that their troops are involved.

Ethnic Banyamulenge Tutsis launched the war after Zairean authorities denied them citizenship and planned to expel them to Rwanda, their ancestral home. They now hold towns and territory along the border with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda.
